documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy for Undergraduate Students (Navigating Artificial Intelligence)
documents.stance_why: The page says 'unauthorized use of artificial intelligence' is plagiarism and bans AI on assessments and as submitted work 'without permission from the instructor' or 'contrary to instructions from the instructor'. It sets no AI rule itself but hands permission to instructors, so delegates, with an integrity-based default ban absent instructor permission.
documents.summary: The Provost's undergraduate academic integrity page defines unauthorized use of AI as plagiarism and misconduct. AI is barred on assessments and as submitted work unless the instructor permits it, so instructors decide. The rest of the page lists general cheating, plagiarism and collaboration rules.

units.why: The sentence classes 'unauthorized use of artificial intelligence' as plagiarism and so as academic misconduct, which is P36 (misuse as misconduct); it binds everyone under the integrity policy, so actor is all and phase when-misuse.
units.anchor: plagiarism (including unauthorized use of artificial intelligence)

units.why: The guideline lists prohibited behaviors for students and says 'Students should refrain from the following', so this is a student-directed scope statement for the list that follows; framework type P56 fits as it sets the purpose and scope of the guideline.
units.anchor: summarize the prohibited behaviors for students while engaged in academic scholarship

units.why: Banning AI in tests 'without permission from the instructor' makes AI on assessments off by default unless the instructor permits; this is P22 (no AI on exams), with permission-by-instructor being the exception.
units.anchor: in taking quizzes, tests, examinations, or other assessments without permission from the instructor
units.frag_start: use of artificial intelligence tools or

units.why: Submitting work 'as one's own' that was produced 'in material or substantial part' by AI without permission is the ban on having AI produce submitted work (P19), chosen over P29 because it is specifically about AI generation.
units.anchor: submitting work for evaluation as one’s own that was produced in material or substantial part
units.fit_note: The ban is tied to 'material or substantial part' and to missing instructor permission, so minor or permitted AI help is not barred.

units.why: Using AI 'contrary to instructions from the instructor' makes the instructor's course or assignment instructions binding on AI use, which is P04 (instructor sets the rule).
units.anchor: in a manner contrary to instructions from the instructor
units.frag_start: using artificial intelligence tools or other

units.why: Using AI in a way that 'violates any other provision' of the dishonesty rules ties AI use to the other integrity rules, matching P77 (comply with existing university policy).
units.anchor: in a manner that violates any other provision of these rules concerning academic dishonesty
units.frag_start: using artificial intelligence tools or other

units.why: The general cheating definition bans 'unauthorized assistance' on assessments, which covers AI assistance without naming it; I code it P22 since it concerns quizzes, tests and exams, though AI is not named.
units.anchor: use of any unauthorized assistance or source in taking quizzes, tests, examinations
units.fit_note: AI is not named; the rule bans any unauthorized assistance or source on assessments.

units.why: Using 'sources beyond those authorized by the instructor in writing' requires instructor authorization for outside sources on assignments, a rule that applies to AI; it is P04 because the instructor decides what is authorized.
units.anchor: sources beyond those authorized by the instructor in writing papers
units.frag_start: use of or referral to sources beyond
units.fit_note: AI is not named; the rule covers any source beyond what the instructor authorizes.

units.why: The plagiarism definition says use of another source 'without properly crediting' is plagiarism; for AI this implies citation, but AI is not named, so disclosure type P24 fits only partly.
units.anchor: without properly crediting the author or source with footnotes, citations or bibliographical reference
units.frag_start: use by paraphrase or direct quotation of
units.fit_note: General plagiarism citation rule; AI is not named, so it applies to AI only by implication.

units.why: Collaboration is dishonest 'unless the instructor explicitly states otherwise'; a default-prohibited rule for collaboration, not AI, but it sets the fallback-when-silent pattern (P06). AI is not named, so I flag the fit.
units.anchor: Unless the instructor explicitly states otherwise, it is dishonest to collaborate with others
units.frag_start: Unless the instructor explicitly states otherwise
units.fit_note: Fallback rule is about collaboration with others, not AI; AI is not named.

units.why: Where group work is allowed only in some cases, 'it is the student's responsibility to understand' the allowed degree and ask; this is P10 (ask when unsure), about collaboration rather than AI.
units.anchor: it is the student’s responsibility to understand the degree of acceptable collaboration
units.frag_start: If the instructor allows group work in
units.fit_note: About collaboration on assignments; AI is not named.

units.why: A signed submission is 'a written statement that credit for the work belongs to that student alone', which is the rule that students own what they submit (P29).
units.anchor: this is a written statement that credit for the work belongs to that student alone

units.why: The rule that students must 'clearly acknowledge in writing all persons who contributed' sets disclosure for collaboration; P24 is the nearest type though AI is not named.
units.anchor: each student is expected to clearly acknowledge in writing all persons who contributed

units.frag_end: persons who contributed to its completion
units.fit_note: Acknowledgement of human collaborators; AI is not named.

units.why: The scope note says the policy applies to undergraduates in all schools and master's students in named schools, which sets who the policy covers; P56 (framework and scope) fits.
units.anchor: applies to undergraduate students enrolled in all Schools and programs
